catalog.title: The Bureaucracy
catalog.description: Municipal, cadastral, archive, notary, and translation routes through one determined folder — now with more offices, more stamps, and considerably more ways to lose an afternoon.
catalog.contentNotice: Satirical depictions of public offices, administrative failure, bribery-adjacent humor, and financial frustration.

strings.bureaucracy.ach.it_builds_character.desc: Reach any resolution after the offices have tested every available kind of patience — and a few kinds you didn't know you had.

strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_1.listen: Write down the guard's room numbers
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_1.text: The guard sends you through civil registry, down one floor, and twenty-seven years backward, past a door numbered in a system that predates the euro, the lev redenomination, and possibly the guard.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_2.improvise: Visit the notary without calling ahead
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_2.prepare: Ask the translator to explain the mismatch
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_2.text: The archive catalog lists your file under a spelling used exactly once, by a tired typist in 1987, who could not have known she was creating a legal identity.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_3.favour: Call in the favour you earned
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_3.favour_fail: No one owes you that favour yet.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_3.text: A translation office can certify the old spelling if a notary certifies that the new spelling is yours — a notary who, coincidentally, is the translator's brother-in-law.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_4.text: The recovered folder reaches a lawyer whose calm costs less than another week of queues and considerably more than lunch.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_event_1.text: The day contributes its own amendment.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_event_1a.text: The handwritten index contains a cross-reference in immaculate blue ink, written by someone who clearly loved this job in a way nobody has since.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_event_1b.text: The database returns nine citizens, two streets, and a livestock permit — none of them relevant, all of them printed anyway.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_event_2.text: A seeded interruption arrives on schedule.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_event_2a.proce: Let the lawyer carry the folder
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_event_2a.text: The translator turns out to know the notary personally and reschedules the appointment before it can disappear a second time.
strings.bureaucracy.archive_route_event_2b.text: Room 14 sends you to Room 6. Room 6 has been repainted, renumbered, and relocated, but the woman behind the desk still remembers the arrangement.
strings.bureaucracy.campaign.description: A municipal casebook through cadastral, tax, registry, archive, notary, and translation offices — and, on a bad day, one very confused European Commission auditor.
strings.bureaucracy.campaign.title: The Bureaucracy
strings.bureaucracy.ending_archive_reveals_secon:
A Discovery Nobody Requested

The old spelling in your file belongs to a second household your great-grandfather apparently maintained two villages over. The archivist finds this considerably more interesting than your paperwork and insists on discussing it at length.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_became_the_archives_h:
The Index You Fixed

You cross-reference the misfiled spelling so thoroughly that the archivist adopts your correction as the new official entry. Your name enters the municipal record twice: once as a citizen, once as a footnote.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_bribed_with_coffee.te:
A Small Coffee, Understood Correctly

You offer to 'buy the clerk a coffee.' Everyone involved understands this is not about coffee. An envelope changes hands beneath a folder, the folder changes hands above the desk, and the file that took two years to lose takes four minutes to find.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_document_obtained.tex:
Document Obtained

The paper arrives with three seals and no apology. It proves the fact everyone already knew before breakfast.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_gave_up.text:
The Folder in the Cupboard

You put the folder away. The municipality records no defeat; it simply stops hearing from you, which it appears to consider a form of resolution.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_hired_a_professional_:
Bay Ivan Queues For You

A retired railway conductor named bay Ivan offers to hold your place for a small daily fee and a standing invitation to your name day. He is better at this than you ever were, has been since 1987, and retires you from the whole process.
A Number, Not a Document

What you receive is an входящ номер — official proof that you asked. It is not the document. It is, several colleagues assure you, 'basically the same thing,' and after seven months you have started to believe them.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_lawyer_solved.text:
Counsel for the Living

The lawyer submits one precise letter. The system, confronted at last with grammar, yields.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_miracle.text:
The Administrative Miracle

The clerk remembers your courtesy, finds the missing entry, and performs an act future staff will swear was never possible.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_promoted_to_the_commi:
A Seat on the Working Group

Impressed by how thoroughly you understand your own case, the municipality invites you to join an informal working group on 'process improvement.' You accept, mostly to make sure this happens to someone else next time.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_reorganized_into_none:
Absorbed Into a New Ministry

Midway through your fourth visit, the office is merged into a newly created Agency for Something Adjacent. Your folder is 'in transition' — a phrase that, you slowly learn, means forever.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_supervisor_adopts_you:
You Become a Personal Project

The supervisor takes a genuine, slightly alarming interest in your file, phones three colleagues by first name, and resolves in one afternoon what four departments failed to resolve in four years. You never learn why. You do not ask.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_system_failure.text:
System Failure, Human Success

The registry crashes while everyone is watching. The supervisor signs a paper fallback last used before Wi-Fi existed in this building.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_the_case_outlives_the:
Reassigned, Indefinitely

The supervisor is transferred to a different department before signing anything. Her successor asks you to start again from Room 1 — this time with a folder thick enough to be taken seriously on its own.
strings.bureaucracy.ending_ultimate_reward.text:
The Ultimate Bulgarian Reward

After seven years of paperwork, you receive €300 and twenty-eight years of unresolved legal responsibility. Somewhere, this counts as closure.
strings.bureaucracy.municipality.choice_ask_guar: Ask the guard for the unofficial route
strings.bureaucracy.municipality.choice_coffee: Get coffee and find the supervisor
strings.bureaucracy.municipality.text: You arrive at the municipality at 08:03. The office opened at 08:00. A handwritten note taped to the glass says the working day ends at 11:30 'for technical reasons'; three nearby doors disagree about which year it currently is.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_1.listen: Thank the clerk and note the expiry date
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_1.text: A clerk unfolds your file like a fortune teller and circles, in red, the one certificate that expires the day after tomorrow — the only day it could possibly have mattered.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_2.improvise: Bring the tax receipt you already have
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_2.text: The cadastral office recognizes the address. The tax office recognizes the building. Neither recognizes the other's right to exist, and both would like this in writing.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_3.favour: Call in the favour you earned
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_3.favour_fail: No one owes you that favour yet.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_3.text: The tax desk needs proof the property exists before it can explain why it owes tax on existing. The proof, naturally, is held one floor up, by an office currently at lunch.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_4.text: Back at the registry, your folder has grown thick enough to command professional respect. The final stamp is now purely a matter of locating whoever still has the stamp.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_event_1.text: The day contributes its own amendment.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_event_1a.text: The pencilled checklist names the one copying shop across the street whose stamp faces the correct direction — everyone knows it, nobody explains it.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_event_1b.text: The official checklist omits a certificate the official who printed it now requires in person.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_event_2.text: A seeded interruption arrives on schedule.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_event_2a.proc: Ask the tax clerk to call upstairs
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_event_2a.text: The tax clerk reaches the cadastral desk by phone and both discover a shared cousin in Sliven.
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_event_2b.proc: Queue again with a fresh number
strings.bureaucracy.registry_route_event_2b.text: Your number is called during the twelve seconds you spend reading the display board instead of watching it.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_1.listen: Let the supervisor finish her coffee
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_1.text: At the café next door you meet a deputy supervisor who remembers your case and, more dangerously, promises to look at it personally.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_2.improvise: Add another certificate just in case
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_2.text: The civil registry accepts the promise as evidence; the translation office would prefer it in writing, ideally with a second, unrelated stamp.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_3.favour: Call in the favour you earned
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_3.favour_fa: No one owes you that favour yet.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_3.text: A notary reviews the growing stack of paper and asks the only genuinely useful question anyone has asked you all day.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_4.ending_pr: A Seat on the Working Group
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_4.text: The supervisor convenes three desks around one shared computer. Either the case resolves, or the system finally, publicly describes what it actually objects to.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_event_1.tex: The day contributes its own amendment.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_event_1a.te: The supervisor writes her direct extension on a napkin — the municipality's most durable and least searchable medium.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_event_1b.te: Your complete seven-year chronology earns a second coffee, sincere sympathy, and no measurable progress whatsoever.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_event_2.tex: A seeded interruption arrives on schedule.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_event_2a.pr: Bring everyone to the same counter
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_event_2a.te: The email arrives with a subject line so alarming that three offices become cooperative within the hour.
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_event_2b.pr: Submit separate copies to each desk
strings.bureaucracy.supervisor_route_event_2b.te: The extra certificate, added purely for safety, contradicts a form nobody had actually read until just now.
